title: Canada beats Finland 2-0, stays perfect heading into women's worlds quarterfinals
summary: Canada completed the preliminary round at the women's ice hockey world championship with a perfect record after blanking Finland 2-0 on Wednesday.

image.caption: Canadian players, pictured on Monday, wrapped up preliminary play at the women's ice hockey world championship with a perfect record after blanking Finland 2-0 on Wednesday. (Ida Marie Odgaard/Ritzau Scanpix via AP)

blocks.text: Canada completed the preliminary round at the women's ice hockey world championship with a perfect record after blanking Finland 2-0 on Wednesday.
Canada will face Czechia in Friday's quarterfinals

Caitlin Kraemer and Sarah Fillier scored, and Ann-Renee Desbiens made 25 saves as Canada finished the group stage of the world women's hockey championship with a perfect record, beating Finland 2-0 on Wednesday.
Finland provided by far the toughest opponent in Group B for Canada, which won its previous three games by a combined score of 24-1 while heavily outshooting the competition.

"It was a big step up from the last couple of games," Kramer said. "We knew Finland would come at us hard, with their usual intensity and aggressiveness. There were some ups and downs, but we stuck together and got the win."
Kraemer opened the scoring at 3:22 of the first period, but Canada wouldn't get any breathing room until Fillier's goal at 6:44 of the third.

Finnish goaltender Sanni Ahola kept her team in the game, making 36 saves.

"It was a good game, two good teams playing hard. We made a couple of tiny mistakes, and they scored right away," said Finnish forward Petra Nieminen, a draft pick of the PWHL's Montreal Victoire. "We take a lot of positives with us from this game, and we want to keep going."
Canada will face Czechia in Friday's quarterfinals. Finland finished third in Group B and will play Germany, who finished a surprising second in Group A.
The other quarterfinals will see Sweden take on Switzerland and the defending champion United States face host Denmark.
The Canadians won silver at last year's championship, losing 4-3 to the United States in overtime.
The Finns put Canada's defence under pressure early, but Kraemer opened the scoring on a two-on-one. Ahola got a piece of Kraemer's wrist shot, but the puck trickled into the net.
"I got off the shot, and somehow it trickled in," Kraemer said.

blocks.text: Desbiens came up big for Canada early in the third, stopping two excellent chances from Nieminen.
Fillier finally gave Canada some relief when she took a pass from Jessie Eldridge, stormed down the right wing and beat Ahola.
Eldridge ended the game tied for second in tournament scoring with seven points, two behind American star Caroline Harvey.
